subject: Mixed (Real Weightage)
description: 100 questions following the real PGP-CET 2025 subject weightage. Mix: 63 easy / 37 medium / 0 hard. Every question cites its source.

questions.question: The commonest white blood cell in adult peripheral blood is the:
questions.explanation: Neutrophils (40–75%), lymphocytes (20–45%), monocytes (2–10%), eosinophils (1–6%), basophils (<1%).
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: Angina pectoris from myocardial ischaemia is classically described as:

options.A: A sharp, localized pain that worsens specifically on inspiration
options.B: A dull, central, retrosternal gripping or band-like sensation that may radiate to the arm, neck, or jaw
options.C: A superficial pain reproduced by chest wall palpation
options.D: A pain confined strictly to the left shoulder with no central component

questions.explanation: Angina pectoris characteristically produces a dull, central, retrosternal gripping or band-like sensation, which may radiate to either arm, the neck, or the jaw — quite distinct from the sharp, localized, movement/palpation-related pain of musculoskeletal chest pain.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Type I (immediate) hypersensitivity is mediated by:
questions.explanation: Anaphylaxis, asthma and hay fever; type IV is delayed (tuberculin test).
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: The immediate response of cutaneous blood vessels to application of ice is:

options.C: A rise in blood pressure only

questions.explanation: Cold causes reflex and direct vasoconstriction, reducing blood flow, oedema formation and metabolism.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The wire used in a fuse should have:

options.A: A very high melting point so that it never breaks
options.B: Magnetic properties so it can switch off the circuit
options.C: A very low resistance and a high thermal tolerance
options.D: A low melting point, so it melts when excess current flows

questions.explanation: A fuse is a deliberate weak link: its low-melting-point wire heats and melts when the current exceeds the rated value, breaking the circuit and protecting the apparatus and patient.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Frenkel's exercises are used to treat:

options.C: Ataxia (incoordination) due to proprioceptive or cerebellar loss

questions.explanation: Frenkel's exercises are graded, repeated, precisely controlled movements performed in lying, sitting and standing with visual feedback.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: In osteoporosis the bone shows:

options.C: Reduced bone mass with normal mineral content per unit of bone

questions.explanation: Osteomalacia is defective mineralisation; Paget's is disorganised remodelling.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: Sickle cell anaemia results from a point mutation in the:
questions.explanation: Autosomal recessive; crises triggered by hypoxia and dehydration.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: A patient with a complete C7 lesion can usually achieve which of the following?

options.B: Independent transfers and wheelchair propulsion on level surfaces

questions.explanation: Triceps and latissimus dorsi allow depression transfers; C7–C8 patients are independent in most self-care.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Vibrations are applied to the chest wall:
questions.explanation: Compressive vibration synchronised with expiration helps move secretions; the force is gentle and the hands stay in contact.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.topic: Electrical Stimulation of Nerve and Muscle
questions.question: A faradic-type current is best defined as:

options.B: A short-duration interrupted direct current with a pulse duration of 0.1-1 ms and a frequency of 50-100 Hz
options.C: A current only used for denervated muscle
options.D: A current with pulse durations always exceeding 100 ms

questions.explanation: A faradic-type current is a short-duration interrupted direct current with a pulse duration of 0.1-1 ms and a frequency of 50-100 Hz — modern electronic stimulators reproduce the same physiological effects as the original faradic coil, just via a different circuit mechanism.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy
questions.sourceChapter: Electrical Stimulation of Nerve and Muscle — Faradic-Type Current
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: A second-class lever has:

options.A: The resistance between the axis and the effort
options.B: The effort between the axis and resistance
options.C: The axis between effort and resistance

questions.explanation: Example: plantar flexion rising on the toes; it favours force (mechanical advantage greater than 1).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Gastrocnemius recession (resection) is most commonly performed in:

options.D: Equinus deformity due to tendo-Achilles tightness

questions.explanation: Used in CTEV and cerebral palsy with equinus.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: Newton's first law of motion (law of inertia) states that:

options.B: Energy cannot be created or destroyed
options.C: A body remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted on by an external force
options.D: Every action has an equal and opposite reaction

questions.explanation: Inertia is the resistance to change in motion; it is proportional to mass.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: The tendo calcaneus (Achilles) is formed by the tendons of:

options.A: Tibialis posterior and flexor hallucis longus

questions.explanation: It inserts on the posterior surface of the calcaneus.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: The gait cycle begins with:

options.C: Heel strike (initial contact) of one foot

questions.explanation: The cycle is divided into stance (60%) and swing (40%) phases.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: The frequencies commonly used in therapeutic ultrasound are:
questions.explanation: 1 MHz penetrates deeper (about 3–5 cm); 3 MHz is absorbed in the superficial 1–2 cm.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The first carpometacarpal joint of the thumb is a:
questions.explanation: Allows flexion/extension, abduction/adduction and opposition.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: The natural pacemaker of the heart is the:
questions.explanation: SA node discharges at 70–80/min; AV node about 40–60/min.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: A clean-contaminated wound is one in which:

options.A: A hollow viscus is entered under controlled conditions without significant spillage
options.B: A sterile elective operation is performed with no viscus entered
options.D: There is a traumatic wound more than 12 hours old

questions.explanation: Clean-contaminated: respiratory, alimentary or genitourinary tract entered under controlled conditions (e.g. elective cholecystectomy). Dirty wounds involve existing infection.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: Pulmonary tuberculosis is mainly transmitted by:
questions.explanation: DOTS is the treatment strategy; sputum smear microscopy is the key diagnostic test.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: In effleurage, the hands move:

options.A: In the direction of venous and lymphatic flow towards the heart

questions.explanation: Effleurage is stroking used to start and finish massage; deep effleurage aids venous return.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: Good standing posture is best described as:

options.C: Any position held for one minute
options.D: The position in which the least muscular effort is needed to maintain body alignment

questions.explanation: Good posture minimises stress on joints and ligaments and uses minimal muscular energy.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: The manoeuvre used to treat posterior canal benign paroxysmal positional vertigo is the:
questions.explanation: Dix–Hallpike is the diagnostic test; Epley (canalith repositioning) is therapeutic.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The most severe form of spina bifida with herniation of both meninges and neural tissue is:
questions.explanation: Myelomeningocele is associated with Arnold–Chiari II malformation, hydrocephalus and variable paralysis.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Which structure is the primary static support of the medial longitudinal arch?

options.A: Plantar calcaneonavicular (spring) ligament and plantar aponeurosis

questions.explanation: Tibialis posterior is the main dynamic support; the arch is also supported by the long plantar ligament and the windlass mechanism of the plantar fascia.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: In most right-handed people, which cerebral hemisphere is specialized for language functions?

options.C: Both hemispheres equally, with no lateralization
options.D: Neither — language is controlled entirely by the cerebellum

questions.explanation: In roughly 95% of right-handed people (and about 65% of left-handed people), the left hemisphere is specialized for language functions, as shown by sodium-amytal testing and by the much higher rate of language problems following left-hemisphere strokes.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology
questions.sourceChapter: Biology of Behavior — Left- and Right-Hemisphere Functions
questions.subject: Psychology

questions.question: An absolute contraindication to spinal manipulation is:

options.A: Mechanical low back pain without red flags
options.C: Cauda equina syndrome or spinal cord compression

questions.explanation: Red flags such as cauda equina syndrome, fracture, infection, malignancy and vertebrobasilar insufficiency contraindicate thrust techniques.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Femoral hernias are more common in:

options.B: Women, and have a high risk of strangulation

questions.explanation: The narrow neck of the femoral canal predisposes to strangulation.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: In the standing human body in anatomical position, the centre of gravity lies approximately:

options.A: Anterior to the second sacral vertebra

questions.explanation: Approximately 55% of standing height (just anterior to S2); it changes with posture.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Which special test is specifically associated with assessing patellofemoral (patellar) instability?
questions.explanation: The apprehension test is used to assess for patellar instability — the examiner laterally displaces the patella and observes for a look or feeling of apprehension from the patient, who fears the patella is about to dislocate.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 12: Knee — Special Tests Commonly Performed on the Knee
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: The Apgar score assesses all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Components: appearance, pulse, grimace, activity, respiration (scored 0–2 each); recorded at 1 and 5 minutes.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: The stretch reflex (knee jerk) is a:
questions.explanation: Muscle spindle Ia afferent synapses directly on the alpha motor neurone.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: Pitting oedema due to heart failure is typically:
questions.explanation: Nephrotic oedema is often periorbital in the morning.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: The best definitive management of a severe flail chest with respiratory failure is:

options.A: Positive pressure ventilation (internal pneumatic stabilisation) with analgesia

questions.explanation: Paradoxical movement is managed by analgesia, oxygen and ventilation if needed; binders restrict breathing.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: The ABCDE approach (Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability, Exposure) used in critically ill patients is an example of which error-reduction strategy?
questions.explanation: ABCDE is probably the most widely used mnemonic/checklist in medicine, reducing reliance on fallible memory and ensuring important issues are considered systematically, especially under stress, complexity, or fatigue.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine
questions.sourceChapter: Clinical Decision Making — Mnemonics and Checklists
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: Which pulse is commonly palpated at the wrist on the radial side?
questions.explanation: Radial pulse at the wrist; brachial in the antecubital fossa; carotid in the neck; femoral in the groin; popliteal behind the knee.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: The most common bone fractured during birth (birth injury) is the:
questions.explanation: Clavicle fracture occurs in difficult deliveries (shoulder dystocia) and heals well with minimal treatment.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: A harsh crescendo-decrescendo systolic murmur radiating to the carotids is characteristic of:
questions.explanation: Triad of aortic stenosis: angina, syncope, dyspnoea.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: In a step-up transformer:

options.A: The primary coil has more turns than the secondary coil
options.B: Direct current is stepped up with no change in turns
options.C: Primary and secondary have equal turns
options.D: The secondary coil has more turns than the primary coil

questions.explanation: Voltage across the secondary ∝ number of secondary turns. A step-up transformer has more secondary turns; it works only with changing (alternating) current.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Which structure is NOT found in a typical synovial joint?

options.B: A fibrocartilage interposed fully between bones without synovial membrane

questions.explanation: Synovial joints have a cavity with synovial fluid, articular hyaline cartilage and capsule.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: A 'restrictive' spirometry pattern, usually associated with reduced lung volume, is characterised by:

options.A: Simultaneous reduction of both FEV1 and FVC, with an INCREASED FEV1/FVC ratio
options.B: Reduction in FEV1 only, with FVC completely unaffected
options.C: No change in spirometry values at all
options.D: An increased FVC with a normal FEV1

questions.explanation: A restrictive pattern shows simultaneous reduction of both FEV1 and FVC together, with an increased FEV1/FVC ratio (since the lungs are small and empty quickly) — distinct from the obstructive pattern where FEV1 drops disproportionately more than FVC.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Ulcerative colitis typically affects the:

options.B: Rectum and extends proximally in continuity

questions.explanation: Crohn's disease: transmural, skip lesions, anywhere from mouth to anus.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: The standard deviation is a measure of:

options.C: Dispersion (spread) of data around the mean

questions.explanation: SD is the square root of variance; in a normal distribution, mean ± 2 SD includes about 95% of values.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: Rice-water stools are characteristic of:
questions.explanation: Vibrio cholerae toxin causes profuse watery diarrhoea; ORS is life-saving.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: Thromboangiitis obliterans (Buerger's disease) is strongly associated with:
questions.explanation: Segmental inflammatory occlusion of medium and small arteries and veins of the limbs.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: The active form of vitamin D is:
questions.explanation: Hydroxylation in the liver (25) and kidney (1α).
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Biochemistry

questions.question: The most effective drug for symptomatic treatment of Parkinson's disease is:
questions.explanation: Levodopa is converted to dopamine; carbidopa prevents peripheral breakdown. Long-term use may cause on-off fluctuations and dyskinesias.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The Functional Independence Measure (FIM) scores each item from:
questions.explanation: FIM has 18 items (13 motor, 5 cognitive) scored 1 (total assistance) to 7 (complete independence).
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Corticosteroid therapy (e.g. methylprednisolone) used to treat acute MS relapses primarily works to:

options.B: Shorten the duration of the acute exacerbation through anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive effects, without modifying the overall disease course
options.C: Cure the underlying autoimmune process entirely
options.D: Have no measurable clinical effect on relapses

questions.explanation: Corticosteroids like methylprednisolone reduce inflammation and suppress immune activity, shortening the duration of an acute relapse — but they do NOT modify the overall disease course or degree of long-term recovery.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan, Physical Rehabilitation
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 16: Multiple Sclerosis — Management of Acute Relapses
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Contralateral hemiparesis and sensory loss that affects the face and arm more than the leg is characteristic of occlusion of the:
questions.explanation: MCA supplies the lateral cortex (face and arm areas of the motor/sensory homunculus); ACA infarction affects the leg more (medial surface).
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: A patient who says 'I often feel anxious in general' is describing which type of anxiety?
questions.explanation: Trait anxiety is a habitual tendency to be anxious in general ('I often feel anxious'), as opposed to state anxiety, which is the anxiety felt at a specific, present, cross-sectional moment ('I feel anxious now'). People with trait anxiety often experience episodes of state anxiety.
questions.sourceBook: Ahuja, A Short Textbook of Psychiatry
questions.sourceChapter: Neurotic, Stress-related and Somatoform Disorders — Anxiety Disorder
questions.subject: Psychiatry

questions.question: A binding site that attaches a drug but produces no pharmacological response at all (e.g. many plasma protein binding sites) is best termed a:

options.B: Silent receptor (or drug acceptor / site of loss)

questions.explanation: Sites that bind a drug without producing any response are called silent receptors, or more accurately drug acceptors / sites of loss — the term 'receptor' is best reserved for binding sites capable of generating an actual biological response.
questions.sourceBook: KD Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology
questions.sourceChapter: Mechanism of Drug Action; Receptor Pharmacology
questions.subject: Pharmacology

questions.question: Which treatment can be injected focally to reduce spasticity in selected muscles?
questions.explanation: Botulinum toxin blocks acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction; effects last about 3 months and should be combined with therapy.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The average age of menarche in India is about:
questions.explanation: Menopause occurs at about 45–50 years.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: To stimulate cough by tracheal stimulation the therapist places a finger:

options.A: Over the thyroid cartilage with hard pressure
options.B: Just above the suprasternal notch, pressing gently on the trachea

questions.explanation: A short gentle pressure at the suprasternal notch can elicit cough in patients who cannot cough voluntarily.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: The WHO (1948) defines health as:

options.D: A state of complete physical, mental and social well-being, not merely the absence of disease or infirmity

questions.explanation: Later definitions added the capacity to lead a socially and economically productive life.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: A tension pneumothorax presents with:

options.C: Tracheal deviation toward the affected side
options.D: Tracheal deviation away from the affected side, hypotension and absent breath sounds

questions.explanation: A one-way valve increases intrapleural pressure and compresses the mediastinum; requires immediate needle decompression.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: The FITT principle in exercise prescription stands for:
questions.explanation: Prescribe frequency (days/week), intensity (% HRmax or 1-RM), time (duration) and type of exercise.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: In shoulder impingement syndrome, the tendon most commonly compressed under the acromion is that of:
questions.explanation: The supraspinatus tendon and subacromial bursa are pinched between the humeral head and coracoacromial arch during abduction/flexion.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: In infants, chest physiotherapy by percussion is performed using:

options.A: Two or three fingers or a small cupped mask, with gentle force
options.C: A mechanical vibrator over the spine
options.D: A cupped adult hand with heavy pressure

questions.explanation: Infants have compliant ribs; gentle techniques with head-down tilt only if medically indicated.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Vitamin D synthesis in the skin results from exposure to:
questions.explanation: 7-dehydrocholesterol in the skin is converted by UVB into cholecalciferol (vitamin D3).
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Mycobacterium tuberculosis is identified by:
questions.explanation: Mycolic acid in the cell wall resists decolourisation by acid.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: A mallet finger results from rupture or avulsion of the:

options.B: Central slip at the PIP joint
options.C: Extensor tendon at its insertion on the distal phalanx
options.D: Collateral ligament of the MCP joint

questions.explanation: Loss of terminal extensor insertion leaves the DIP joint flexed and unable to extend actively. Treated by splinting the DIP in extension for about 6–8 weeks.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: When a patient develops a clinically suspected deep vein thrombosis the physiotherapist should:

options.A: Stop exercise of the limb, rest, and refer for urgent medical assessment
options.D: Apply heat and give vigorous exercise

questions.explanation: Exercise or massage may dislodge a thrombus, causing pulmonary embolism.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Which carpal bone is described as the largest, with a rounded head, occupying the centre of the distal row?
questions.explanation: The capitate is the largest carpal bone, identified by its rounded head, and sits in the distal row.
questions.sourceBook: BD Chaurasia's Human Anatomy — Upper Limb
questions.sourceChapter: Bones of the Upper Limb — Carpal Bones
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: The hormone detected in a urine pregnancy test is:
questions.explanation: hCG is produced by the syncytiotrophoblast; levels double every 48 hours in early pregnancy.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: Stridor is often mistakenly called 'wheeze' by patients, but it actually indicates:
questions.explanation: Stridor is the sound produced by upper airway obstruction and is often mistakenly labelled 'wheeze' by patients, though true wheeze arises from turbulent airflow through narrowed lower airways — an important clinical distinction.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: A muscle that completes the full available range against gravity but cannot tolerate any added resistance is graded:
questions.explanation: Grade 3 (Fair) = full range against gravity without resistance. Grade 4 tolerates moderate resistance, grade 5 maximal resistance.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: The most common type of scoliosis seen in adolescents is:
questions.explanation: About 80% of structural scoliosis is idiopathic; adolescent idiopathic scoliosis is more common in girls.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: The most common complication after a Colles' fracture is:

options.A: Stiffness of the fingers and wrist

questions.explanation: Stiffness from prolonged immobilisation and oedema is the commonest complication; others include malunion, EPL rupture and Sudeck's atrophy (complex regional pain syndrome).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: The causative organism of tetanus is:
questions.explanation: A gram-positive anaerobic spore-bearer; tetanospasmin blocks inhibitory neurotransmitters, causing trismus and risus sardonicus.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: The weakest current intensity that produces a minimal visible muscle contraction when applied for an indefinitely long pulse duration is called:
questions.explanation: Rheobase is the minimum intensity (of a long-duration stimulus) that evokes a threshold response. Chronaxie is the pulse duration needed at twice the rheobase.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Which artery occlusion typically produces contralateral leg weakness greater than arm weakness, with abulia and urinary incontinence?
questions.explanation: ACA supplies the medial frontal and parietal lobes, including the leg area and paracentral lobule; frontal lobe signs include abulia and grasp reflex.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Rickets in children is due to deficiency of:
questions.explanation: Sunlight exposure and supplementation prevent it; adults develop osteomalacia.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: The Trendelenburg test is positive when:

options.B: The pelvis drops on the unsupported side while standing on one leg
options.C: The pelvis rises on the unsupported side

questions.explanation: Weak hip abductors on the stance side let the pelvis drop on the opposite side.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: The classical pain of acute appendicitis starts in the:

options.A: Epigastrium and radiates to the shoulder
options.C: Periumbilical region and then localises to the right iliac fossa

questions.explanation: Visceral pain from midgut, then parietal peritoneal irritation at McBurney's point.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: The typical position of the hip in advanced osteoarthritis is:
questions.explanation: OA of the hip produces a capsular pattern (flexion, abduction and medial rotation lost) with a fixed deformity in flexion, adduction and external rotation.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: The principle of overload in strength training states that:

options.A: Muscle strength improves only when it is stressed beyond its normal level of demand
options.B: Exercise must be done to fatigue daily
options.C: Strength improves with light loading only

questions.explanation: Progressive overload of intensity, volume or frequency is required for adaptation.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: McMurray's test is used to detect:
questions.explanation: The knee is flexed, tibia rotated and then extended while palpating the joint line; a click or pain indicates a meniscal lesion.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: A paraffin wax bath at about 50–55 °C does not usually burn the patient because wax has:

options.A: A low specific heat and low thermal conductivity

questions.explanation: Wax has a low specific heat and is a poor conductor, so only a small amount of heat is transferred to the skin; a thin layer solidifies and insulates.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: A firm, leathery end-feel before the normal end of range suggests:
questions.explanation: Firm end-feel = capsular/ligamentous resistance; early muscle spasm gives a ‘springy’ stop; a loose body gives a springy block.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Blood group is an example of which type of variable?
questions.explanation: Nominal: names without order; ordinal: ranked (muscle grade 0–5); interval: equal intervals no true zero (temperature °C); ratio: true zero (height).
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: The classical mechanism of posterior cruciate ligament injury is:

options.A: A valgus force with the foot fixed
options.C: A posteriorly directed force on the proximal tibia (e.g. dashboard injury) with the knee flexed

questions.explanation: Falling on the flexed knee or a dashboard impact drives the tibia backwards, rupturing the PCL; posterior sag sign and posterior drawer are positive.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: The resting membrane potential of a skeletal muscle fibre is approximately:
questions.explanation: Skeletal muscle fibres have a resting potential of about −90 mV, more negative than the −70 mV of nerve.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Conventional TENS is characterised by:

options.A: High frequency (~50–100 Hz) and low (sensory) intensity
options.B: Low frequency and high intensity producing muscle twitches
options.D: Direct current at a very low frequency

questions.explanation: Conventional TENS stimulates large Aβ fibres to activate the pain gate; patients feel a comfortable paraesthesia without muscle contraction.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The resting membrane potential of a nerve fibre is mainly due to:

options.B: Potassium efflux through leak channels and the Na⁺–K⁺ pump

questions.explanation: The membrane is far more permeable to K⁺ at rest; the Na⁺/K⁺ ATPase pumps 3 Na⁺ out and 2 K⁺ in.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: Jacobson's progressive relaxation technique involves:

options.B: Systematic contraction followed by relaxation of different muscle groups

questions.explanation: The patient learns to recognise the difference between tension and relaxation by alternately contracting and relaxing muscle groups.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: Wolff's law states that:

options.A: Bone adapts its structure to the loads placed on it
options.B: Bone growth is independent of load
options.C: Muscle adapts to disuse by hypertrophy

questions.explanation: Increased loading increases bone density; disuse leads to osteopenia.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Aspirin acts by:
questions.explanation: Low-dose aspirin inhibits platelet aggregation by blocking thromboxane A2 synthesis.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pharmacology

questions.question: Sickle cell anaemia is inherited as:
questions.explanation: Heterozygotes (sickle trait) are usually asymptomatic and protected against malaria.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: Froment's sign is a test for:
questions.explanation: When gripping a sheet of paper between thumb and index finger, the thumb IP joint flexes (FPL, median nerve) to compensate for a paralysed adductor pollicis.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Which condition is a contraindication to lumbar or cervical traction?

options.B: Mechanical low back pain with muscle spasm
options.D: Mild lumbar disc protrusion without neurological deficit

questions.explanation: Traction is contraindicated with cord signs, unstable fracture, severe osteoporosis, infection, malignancy, vertebrobasilar insufficiency and acute inflammatory arthritis (e.g. rheumatoid atlantoaxial instability).
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: When a concave joint surface moves on a fixed convex surface, the glide occurs:

options.D: In the same direction as the bone movement

questions.explanation: Concave on convex: glide in the SAME direction as the bone moves. Convex on concave: glide in the OPPOSITE direction.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Which exercise is most appropriate on the first day after a total knee replacement?
questions.explanation: Early isometric quadriceps work, ankle pumps (DVT prevention), and CPM/active-assisted flexion begin immediately within pain limits.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Tracheal suction through an endotracheal tube should be limited in duration to about:
questions.explanation: Prolonged suctioning causes hypoxia, vagal bradycardia and trauma; pre-oxygenate and use sterile technique.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: By convention, when writing a peptide chain, which end is placed on the left?
questions.explanation: Peptide chains are conventionally written with the N-terminal residue (free amino end) on the left and the C-terminal residue (free carboxyl end) on the right; the sequence is read from N-terminal to C-terminal, matching the direction protein biosynthesis proceeds in.
questions.sourceBook: Satyanarayana, Biochemistry
questions.sourceChapter: Proteins and Amino Acids — Peptide Bond
questions.subject: Biochemistry

questions.question: The dermatome that covers the thumb is:
questions.explanation: C6 thumb, C7 middle finger, C8 little finger. T4 nipple, T10 umbilicus.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: The radial nerve supplies all of the following muscles EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Radial nerve: all extensors of the arm and forearm, brachioradialis and supinator.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: Traction applied with a light weight for a prolonged period (hours) is:
questions.explanation: Continuous traction uses small forces for long periods (e.g. in bed rest to rest an area); intermittent traction alternates higher force with rest periods for 10–30 minutes.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy
